title: Deviations, Incomplete Work and Honest Status

content.overview: Cultivation work can deviate from plan. Technicians must preserve factual status, record incomplete work honestly and hand unresolved conditions forward without inventing data or completion.

vocabulary.definition: A documented departure from an approved instruction, expected condition, specification or planned process.
A condition anticipated by a procedure that requires a defined alternate action or approval.
Accurately representing what was done, what was not done and what remains unresolved.

sections.title: Deviations are operational information
sections.body: Equipment faults, identity mismatches, alarms, material shortages, contamination concerns and other conditions can interrupt work. The technician preserves what actually happened rather than forcing the record to appear normal.

sections.title: Never manufacture completion
sections.body: A task is complete only when required steps and acceptance criteria are met or an authorized exception is documented. Missed observations remain missing; they are not reconstructed from guesses or memory and presented as contemporaneous data.

workedExamples: An interrupted sanitation cycle is documented as incomplete instead of being signed complete.
A missed measurement is recorded according to the missing-data procedure rather than invented later.
commonMistakes: Hiding deviations because they feel like personal failure.
Marking work complete simply because the shift ended.
content.practicalApplication: Review a partially completed work packet, identify deviations and incomplete steps, decide what can continue or must stop, and write the handoff status.
content.summary: Reliable operations depend on truthful status. Technicians document deviations and incomplete work as they occurred and make unresolved conditions visible.

blocks.title: A deviation is information, not a confession
blocks.body: Abnormal conditions occur in real operations: equipment faults, identity mismatches, missing material, sanitation interruptions, alarms, access restrictions, and incomplete prior work. The quality problem becomes worse when the record is changed to make the shift appear normal. The technician's job is to preserve the true status so the next decision can be made from reliable facts.

left.label: Truthful status
left.body: The sanitation cycle stopped before the required final step. The record shows the last completed step, the interruption time, the reason, who was notified, and that the task remains incomplete.

right.label: Manufactured completion
right.body: The technician signs the sanitation task complete because most steps were finished and the shift is ending, leaving the next worker to assume the controlled process is closed.

blocks.title: Deviation / incomplete-work handoff
blocks.description: A useful record shows what was expected, what actually happened, and what remains open without turning hypotheses into facts.

fields.label: Affected task / ID
fields.value: Work order, room, plant/material, asset, or process identifier

fields.label: Expected condition
fields.value: What the current instruction or acceptance criterion required

fields.label: Actual condition
fields.value: What was observed or completed, stated factually

fields.label: Time / sequence point
fields.value: When the deviation occurred or the last confirmed completed step

fields.label: Immediate control
fields.value: What was safely stopped, isolated, preserved, or left unchanged under procedure

fields.label: Notification
fields.value: Who or what role was notified and when

fields.label: Open status
fields.value: What remains incomplete, unknown, held, or awaiting decision

fields.label: Next required action
fields.value: Defined follow-up or authorized decision if known

blocks.note: Do not backfill a missed measurement, sign a missed step as complete, or hide an unresolved condition inside general shift notes.

blocks.title: The irrigation task is incomplete when the shift ends
blocks.setting: A scheduled irrigation task stops after an equipment fault. Only two of three assigned zones received the planned event. The next shift starts in 15 minutes.
blocks.prompt: Which closeout best preserves status integrity?
options: Mark the whole task complete because most of it occurred
Enter the planned values for the missed zone so the record is consistent
Record which zones were completed, identify the missed zone and fault context, preserve the open status, and hand off the required next action
Delete the task so the next shift can recreate it
blocks.answer: Record which zones were completed, identify the missed zone and fault context, preserve the open status, and hand off the required next action.
blocks.feedback: A shift boundary does not convert incomplete work into completed work. The next worker needs an accurate starting state.

blocks.title: Close a partially completed work packet
blocks.instructions: Audit a supplied work packet containing one equipment interruption, one missed observation, one completed step, and one unresolved identity issue. Produce a truthful end-of-shift status.
prompts: Mark what is actually complete and identify the evidence for completion.
Identify every incomplete or unknown element without guessing a value.
Write the minimum useful handoff for each open item.
Identify which item blocks downstream work until an authorized decision occurs.

blocks.title: Key takeaway
blocks.body: A trustworthy operation can work with an honest deviation. It cannot reliably work with a false normal record. Preserve what actually happened, what did not happen, and what remains unresolved.
